title: Werkzeug Debugger PIN Exposed in Application Logs
description: The Werkzeug debugger PIN is exposed in the Flask application output log file stored at /tmp/flask_output.log. The log file contains the message "Debugger PIN: 141-511-490" along with other sensitive debugging information and stack traces. This log file is world-readable (permissions: -rw-r--r--) and accessible to any user on the system, completely defeating the purpose of the PIN protection mechanism on the debugger console. The POC successfully extracts the PIN from the log file, demonstrates world-readable permissions, and confirms the presence of additional sensitive information including debug mode indicators and stack traces with file paths.
impact: An attacker can read the Flask log file (/tmp/flask_output.log) to obtain the debugger PIN (141-511-490). Combined with the Werkzeug Debugger SECRET token disclosure vulnerability, an attacker has all the information needed to authenticate to the debugger console and execute arbitrary Python code on the server. The PIN, while intended to prevent unauthorized authentication, is trivially accessible in the local logs to any user with filesystem access. This completely bypasses the intended security protection and enables remote code execution via the interactive Python console.
evidence:
POC Execution Output:
- Log file found at /tmp/flask_output.log with world-readable permissions (-rw-r--r--)
- Debugger PIN successfully extracted: 141-511-490
- Debug mode indicators confirmed in logs: "Debug mode: on", "Debugger is active!"
- WARNING messages present indicating development server in production environment
- 9 stack trace entries with file paths found in log file
- Log file size: 1942 bytes

The POC script successfully demonstrates:
1. Access to world-readable log file
2. Extraction of debugger PIN using grep
3. Confirmation of additional sensitive information in logs
4. Verification that world-readable permissions expose all users to this data
remediation:
1. Never write debugger PINs or other sensitive authentication credentials to log files - implement log sanitization
2. Restrict log file permissions to owner only (chmod 600) to prevent unauthorized access
3. Store logs in secure locations with proper access controls and separate from /tmp directories
4. Disable Flask debug mode in production by setting FLASK_DEBUG=False and DEBUG=False
5. Use centralized logging infrastructure with encryption and access controls instead of local world-readable log files
6. Implement log rotation policies and secure log storage with automatic deletion of old logs
7. Sanitize all log output to exclude sensitive information: PINs, tokens, credentials, stack traces, file paths
8. Implement proper logging levels - use INFO level in production, avoid DEBUG level logs in production
9. Configure Flask to not write debug information to logs - set up proper application logging separate from Werkzeug debug logs
10. Audit all current log files for similar exposures of sensitive information
references: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File; CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password; OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control; OWASP A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
toolCallDescription: Documenting the Werkzeug Debugger PIN exposure vulnerability with successful POC proof of PIN extraction from world-readable log file
